question: Khelo India Winter Games 2023 was held at _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khelo India Winter Games (KIWG) 2023, the third edition, was held at Gulmarg, Jammu and Kashmir, from 24 to 28 February 2023. (खेलो इंडिया विंटर गेम्स — जम्मू और कश्मीर)

 

• The games featured winter sports such as skiing, ice hockey, snowboarding, and ice skating, and were organised under the Khelo India scheme.

 

• Jammu and Kashmir topped the medal tally at the event.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gulmarg has hosted multiple editions of the Khelo India Winter Games, cementing its status as India's premier winter sports hub.

 

• The Khelo India scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2018 to revive sports culture at the grassroots level.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 1): Though a winter sports destination (e.g., Manali, Solang Valley), it did not host the 2023 edition of KIWG.

 

• Leh (Option 3): Leh, Ladakh hosted an earlier edition (Khelo India Winter Games 2021), not the 2023 edition.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 4): Known for winter sports centres like Auli, but it was not the host of KIWG 2023.

question: Which amongst the following Sultans shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq, the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty, shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (renamed Devagiri) in 1327 CE. (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक — दौलताबाद)

 

• The transfer was intended to give him a capital more centrally located to control the Deccan, but it caused massive hardship as the entire population was forced to migrate.

 

• The experiment failed, and he was forced to shift the capital back to Delhi around 1335 CE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq is also known for introducing token currency (copper/brass coins) in place of silver coins, another controversial experiment.

 

• Historian Ishwari Prasad called him an 'ill-starred idealist' due to his ambitious but poorly executed policies.

 

NOTE

 

• Feroz Shah Tughlaq (Option 2): Successor of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, known for welfare works and canal construction, not for shifting the capital.

 

• Sikandar Lodhi (Option 3): Second ruler of the Lodhi dynasty; founded the city of Agra.

 

• Ibrahim Lodhi (Option 4): Last ruler of the Lodhi dynasty, defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

question: As of March, 2024, who is the Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Sanjiv Khanna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of March 2024, Justice Sanjiv Khanna served as the Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), being the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court after the Chief Justice of India. (राष्ट्रीय विधिक सेवा प्राधिकरण — न्यायमूर्ति संजीव खन्ना)

 

• NALSA was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, to provide free legal aid to weaker sections of society and to organise Lok Adalats.

 

• The Chief Justice of India (then Justice D.Y. Chandrachud) serves as the Patron-in-Chief of NALSA, while the senior-most puisne judge of the Supreme Court serves as its Executive Chairman.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Justice Sanjiv Khanna later went on to become the Chief Justice of India in November 2024.

 

• NALSA is headquartered in New Delhi and works through a network of State, District, and Taluk Legal Services Authorities.

 

NOTE

 

• Justice UU Lalit (Option 1): Former CJI (August-November 2022); had already retired well before March 2024.

 

• Justice Ranjan Gogoi (Option 3): Former CJI (2018-2019); retired and later became a Rajya Sabha member.

 

• Justice Sharad Bobde (Option 4): Former CJI (2019-2021); had already retired by March 2024.

question: _________ of the Constitution of India has provisions for legal enforcement of the fundamental rights.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 32.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 32 of the Constitution of India provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, empowering citizens to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. (अनुच्छेद 32 — संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार)

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution, since it is what makes the Fundamental Rights enforceable.

 

• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue five kinds of writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto — to enforce Fundamental Rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 226 grants similar writ jurisdiction to the High Courts, but it is a constitutional (not Fundamental) power, and its scope is wider than Article 32.

 

• Article 32 itself falls within Part III of the Constitution, which lists the Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 28 (Option 1): Deals with freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions.

 

• Article 19 (Option 2): Guarantees six freedoms (speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession) under the Right to Freedom.

 

• Article 29 (Option 4): Protects the right of minorities to conserve their distinct language, script, and culture.

question: Which statement about Classical Carnatic Music is correct?
option_1: The compositions are either in Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil or Bengali.
option_2: The compositions are either in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil or Sanskrit.
option_3: The compositions are either in Telugu, Malayalam, Hindi or Sanskrit.
option_4: The compositions are either in Marathi, Odia, Konkani or Bengali.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The compositions are either in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil or Sanskrit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Classical Carnatic Music, the classical music tradition of South India, has compositions predominantly in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, and Sanskrit. (कर्नाटक संगीत — तेलुगु, कन्नड़, तमिल, संस्कृत)

 

• The Carnatic Trinity — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri — composed extensively in these languages, most famously Tyagaraja's compositions in Telugu.

 

• Carnatic music is characterised by its emphasis on raga (melody) and tala (rhythm), expressed through forms like kritis, varnams, and padams.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindustani classical music, the North Indian tradition, features compositions largely in Hindi, Urdu, and Braj Bhasha.

 

• Institutions like the Madras Music Academy (Chennai) are major centres promoting and preserving Carnatic music.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Bengali): This is not the standard set of Carnatic composition languages.

 

• Option 3 (Telugu, Malayalam, Hindi, Sanskrit): Hindi is not a traditional language of Carnatic compositions.

 

• Option 4 (Marathi, Odia, Konkani, Bengali): None of these are among the principal languages of Carnatic music.

question: Which of the following is NOT compulsory equipment for a football referee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is White flag.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Laws of the Game (Law 4) framed by the IFAB (International Football Association Board), a football referee's compulsory basic equipment includes a whistle, watch(es), and red and yellow cards. (फुटबॉल रेफरी — सफेद झंडा अनिवार्य उपकरण नहीं)

 

• A white flag is not part of the referee's kit — it is the assistant referees (linesmen) who carry flags to signal offside, throw-ins, and fouls, and these flags need not be white.

 

• The whistle is used to start and stop play, the red and yellow cards to caution or dismiss players (introduced at the 1970 FIFA World Cup), and the watch to keep match time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The card system was devised by English referee Ken Aston, inspired by the colours of traffic lights.

 

• Modern top-level referees may additionally use equipment such as vanishing spray and communication devices, though these are not part of the basic mandatory kit.

 

NOTE

 

• Red and yellow cards (Option 1): Compulsory equipment, used for cautioning or sending off players.

 

• Whistle(s) (Option 3): Compulsory equipment, used to start/stop play and signal fouls.

 

• Watch(es) (Option 4): Compulsory equipment, used to track match time.

question: To create a new MS Word document, which of the following steps is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is File Tab → New.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word, to create a new document, the correct sequence is File Tab → New, which opens the New Document pane offering a blank document as well as templates. (माइक्रोसॉफ्ट वर्ड — फाइल टैब न्यू)

 

• The File tab opens the Backstage View, which provides options for creating, opening, saving, printing, and sharing documents.

 

• The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + N is a quick alternative way to create a new blank document directly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• File → Open is used to access an existing saved document, not to create a new one.

 

• File → Save As is used to save a copy of the current document under a new name or location.

 

NOTE

 

• File Tab → Open (Option 1): Opens an existing document; does not create a new one.

 

• File Tab → Start (Option 2): Not a valid command/option in MS Word's File (Backstage) menu.

 

• File Tab → Recent (Option 4): Displays a list of recently opened documents; does not create a new document.

question: Lal Thanhawla holds the record for the longest-serving Chief Minister of ________, occupying the position for five terms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lal Thanhawla holds the record for being the longest-serving Chief Minister of Mizoram, having served five terms as CM (1984-86, 1989-93, 1993-98, 2008-13, 2013-18). (लाल थनहवला — मिजोरम)

 

• He was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and remained a central figure in Mizoram's politics after the state attained statehood in 1987.

 

• He is remembered for steering Mizoram's post-accord peace and development process following the Mizo Accord (1986).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mizoram attained full statehood on 20 February 1987; its first Chief Minister was Laldenga.

 

• Zoramthanga, leader of the Mizo National Front (MNF), is another prominent multi-term Chief Minister of Mizoram.

 

NOTE

 

• Sikkim (Option 1): Its longest-serving CM was Pawan Kumar Chamling (five terms, 1994-2019), not Lal Thanhawla.

 

• Manipur (Option 2): Okram Ibobi Singh served three consecutive terms as CM of Manipur, not Lal Thanhawla.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 4): Lal Thanhawla was never Chief Minister of Meghalaya.

question: Which of the following dances is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kalbelia folk dance of Rajasthan, performed traditionally by the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community, was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• It is characterised by dancers in swirling black skirts moving in serpentine motions, accompanied by instruments like the poongi (been), dholak, and khanjari.

 

• It is one of the most iconic folk dance forms representing the traditional lifestyle of Rajasthan's Kalbelia community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian elements on the UNESCO ICH list include Kutiyattam (2008), Ramlila (2008), Chhau dance (2010), Yoga (2016), and Durga Puja (2021).

 

NOTE

 

• Garba (Option 2): The traditional dance of Gujarat was inscribed on the UNESCO ICH list in 2023, not 2010.

 

• Ghumar (Option 3): A folk dance of Rajasthan; it is not on the UNESCO ICH list.

 

• Matki (Option 4): A folk dance from the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh; it is not on the UNESCO ICH list.

question: The Assam government observed the birthday of ________ on 31 March 2023, as Students Day in the state.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bodofa Upendra Nath Brahma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Assam government declared 31 March as 'Vidyarthi Diwas' (Students' Day) in the state, to mark the birth anniversary of Bodofa Upendra Nath Brahma. (बोडोफा उपेंद्र नाथ ब्रह्म — असम विद्यार्थी दिवस)

 

• Upendra Nath Brahma, popularly known as 'Bodofa' (father of the Bodos), was the founder of the All Bodo Students' Union (ABSU) and a key figure in the Bodo movement.

 

• The Assam cabinet took this decision in March 2023, alongside announcing tuition fee waivers for girl students studying science in Classes XI and XII.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The announcement was made under the Assam government led by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.

 

• ABSU (All Bodo Students' Union) has played a major role in the Bodoland statehood/autonomy movement in Assam.

 

NOTE

 

• Biraj Kumar Sarma (Option 2): Not the person whose birthday was declared Students' Day in Assam.

 

• Prafulla Kumar Mahanta (Option 3): A former Chief Minister of Assam and AASU leader, but this observance is not tied to his birthday.

 

• Bhrigu Kumar Phukan (Option 4): An AASU leader, but this observance is not tied to his birthday.

question: As per the Census-2011, the total absolute increase in population during the decade is ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.19 crore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, 2011, India's population increased from about 102.87 crore (2001) to 121.09 crore (2011), an absolute increase of roughly 18.19 crore during the decade. (जनगणना 2011 — निरपेक्ष जनसंख्या वृद्धि 18.19 करोड़)

 

• The decadal growth rate for 2001-2011 was 17.64%, which was lower than the growth rate of the previous decade (1991-2001: 21.54%) — the first such decline recorded in independent India.

 

• Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest absolute increase in population among all Indian states during this decade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census 2011 recorded India's total population at 1,210,854,977, making India the second most populous country in the world at the time, after China.

 

• The sex ratio improved to 943 females per 1,000 males in 2011, up from 933 in 2001.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (15.23 crore, 17.21 crore, 16.41 crore): These figures do not match the official Census 2011 data on the absolute increase in population.

question: Which of the following is NOT related to the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Purandara Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Trinity of Carnatic Music' refers to three composers — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri — all born in Thiruvarur, Tamil Nadu, in the 18th century. (कर्नाटक संगीत त्रयी — त्यागराज, मुथुस्वामी दीक्षितार, श्यामा शास्त्री)

 

• Purandara Das (15th-16th century) lived much earlier and is honoured as the 'Pitamaha' (grandfather) of Carnatic music for systematising its teaching methodology, but he is NOT counted among the Trinity.

 

• Each member of the Trinity composed prolifically — Tyagaraja mainly in Telugu, Dikshitar largely in Sanskrit, and Syama Sastri in Telugu and Sanskrit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Purandara Das is credited with devising the raga Mayamalavagowla as the foundational scale for teaching Carnatic music, a practice that continues to this day.

 

• The Carnatic Trinity is celebrated annually through the Thyagaraja Aradhana music festival held at Thiruvaiyaru.

 

NOTE

 

• Syama Shastri (Option 1), Tyagaraja (Option 2), Muthuswami Dikshitar (Option 3): All three are genuine members of the Trinity of Carnatic Music.

question: According to Koeppen's Scheme of classification of climate, which of the following characteristics is associated with 'Group E'?
option_1: The average temperature of the coldest month is –3°C or below
option_2: The average temperature of the coldest month is higher than –3°C but below 18°C
option_3: The average temperature of the coldest month is 18°C or higher
option_4: The average temperature for all months is below 10°C
solution_text:
The correct answer is The average temperature for all months is below 10°C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Koeppen's scheme of climate classification, Group E represents the Polar climates, defined by the criterion that the average temperature of all twelve months remains below 10°C. (कोपेन जलवायु वर्गीकरण — समूह E, ध्रुवीय जलवायु)

 

• Group E is further divided into ET (Tundra), where the warmest month averages between 0°C and 10°C, and EF (Ice cap/Frost), where every month averages below 0°C.

 

• Koeppen's scheme, devised by climatologist Wladimir Koeppen, uses letter codes (A, B, C, D, E, H) based on temperature and precipitation patterns to classify world climates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Group A denotes Tropical climates, where the coldest month's average temperature is 18°C or higher.

 

• Group B denotes Dry climates, classified on the basis of precipitation and evaporation rather than temperature alone.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (coldest month –3°C or below): This threshold is used to distinguish Group D (cold/continental) climates, not Group E.

 

• Option 2 (coldest month higher than –3°C but below 18°C): This is the defining criterion of Group C (warm temperate) climates.

 

• Option 3 (coldest month 18°C or higher): This is the defining criterion of Group A (tropical) climates.

question: Doljatra is a festival of which state from followings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Doljatra (also called Dol Utsav/Dol Jatra), the regional form of the Holi festival, is prominently celebrated in Assam, most famously at Barpeta. (डोलजात्रा — असम)

 

• It is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) of the Hindu month of Phalgun (Feb-March), marked by the swinging of deity idols on a decorated swing ('dol') and the play of colours.

 

• The festival is closely associated with the Vaishnavite Sattras established by Srimanta Sankardeva in Assam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Doljatra/Dol Purnima is also celebrated under similar names in West Bengal and Odisha, tied to Vaishnavite tradition.

 

• The Barpeta Dol celebration at the Barpeta Satra is one of Assam's most significant socio-religious festivals, drawing large crowds annually.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 1): Known for festivals like Teej, Gangaur, and the Pushkar Fair, not specifically for Doljatra.

 

• Haryana (Option 3): Known for festivals like Baisakhi and Gugga Naumi; Doljatra is not a native Haryana festival.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Known for Holi celebrations (e.g., Barsana's Lathmar Holi), but these are not referred to as 'Doljatra'.

question: Price control and rationing are direct control measures to check ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is inflation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Price control and rationing are direct control measures used by governments to check inflation, i.e., a sustained rise in the general price level. (मूल्य नियंत्रण और राशनिंग — मुद्रास्फीति नियंत्रण)

 

• Price control involves the government fixing maximum (ceiling) prices for essential goods, while rationing restricts the quantity a consumer can purchase, ensuring equitable distribution during scarcity.

 

• These are direct/administrative measures, as opposed to indirect/monetary measures like changes in the repo rate, CRR, or SLR used by the central bank.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other direct measures to control inflation include export restrictions, import liberalisation, and strengthening the Public Distribution System (PDS).

 

• Monetary (indirect) measures to control inflation are typically employed by the RBI through tools like the repo rate and open market operations.

 

NOTE

 

• Disinflation (Option 1): Refers to a slowdown in the rate of inflation, not the phenomenon that price control/rationing are used to check.

 

• Deflation (Option 2): A sustained fall in the general price level — the opposite of what these measures target.

 

• Reflation (Option 4): A deliberate policy to stimulate the economy by expanding money supply, unrelated to the objective of price control/rationing.

question: Application software includes a variety of programs that are designed to meet the information processing needs of _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is end users.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Application software comprises programs designed to help users perform specific tasks (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, browsing), meeting the information processing needs of end users. (एप्लीकेशन सॉफ्टवेयर — अंतिम उपयोगकर्ता)

 

• It is distinct from system software (such as the operating system), which manages a computer's hardware resources and provides a platform on which application software runs.

 

• Common examples of application software include MS Word, MS Excel, web browsers, and media players.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Application software is broadly classified into general-purpose software (e.g., word processors) and application-specific software (e.g., payroll systems).

 

• Utility software (e.g., antivirus programs, disk cleanup tools) supports system maintenance and is distinct from both system and application software.

 

NOTE

 

• Programmers (Option 1): Primarily use system/programming software (compilers, IDEs) to write programs; they are not the intended audience of application software.

 

• Team leaders (Option 2) and Customers (Option 3): Not the standard technical term used in this context — the correct generic term is 'end users'.

question: Which sport is NOT played in mixed doubles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Handball.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Handball is a team sport, played 7-a-side (6 court players plus 1 goalkeeper), and it does not have a 'mixed doubles' format, unlike racquet sports. (हैंडबॉल — मिश्रित युगल प्रारूप नहीं)

 

• Badminton, Tennis, and Table Tennis are all racquet sports that feature a 'mixed doubles' format, where a team consists of one male and one female player.

 

• Mixed doubles events are regular features at major tournaments such as the Olympics, Grand Slams (tennis), and the BWF World Championships (badminton).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Handball, which originated in Europe in the early 20th century, is an Olympic sport with separate men's and women's team competitions, but no mixed doubles category.

 

• Mixed doubles was introduced as an Olympic event in Table Tennis starting from the Tokyo 2020 Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 2), Tennis (Option 3), Table tennis (Option 4): All are established racquet sports with a recognised mixed doubles category.

question: How many Fundamental Rights were initially provided in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution of India, as originally adopted in 1950, provided for seven Fundamental Rights under Part III. (मूल अधिकार — मूलतः सात)

 

• These were: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, Right to Property, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• The Right to Property (originally Article 31) was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and re-designated as a legal right under Article 300-A, reducing the count to six.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Currently, there are six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under the Constitution of India.

 

• Fundamental Rights are justiciable (enforceable in a court of law), which distinguishes them from the non-justiciable Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

NOTE

 

• Six (Option 1): This is the current number of Fundamental Rights, after the removal of the Right to Property, not the originally provided number.

 

• Nine (Option 2) and Eight (Option 4): Incorrect figures that do not match either the original or the current count of Fundamental Rights.

question: Which of the following is the correct relationship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is F = ma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's Second Law of Motion states that the force acting on a body equals the product of its mass and acceleration, giving the relationship F = ma, where F is force, m is mass, and a is acceleration. (न्यूटन का द्वितीय गति नियम — F = ma)

 

• This relationship defines the SI unit of force, the newton (N): 1 newton is the force required to give a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s² (1 N = 1 kg·m/s²).

 

• It is one of the three laws of motion published by Sir Isaac Newton in his work *Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica* (1687).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's First Law (law of inertia) states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

 

• Newton's Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• F = a/m (Option 1) and F = m/a (Option 2): Dimensionally incorrect rearrangements that do not represent the actual force-mass-acceleration relationship.

 

• F = m²a (Option 3): Dimensionally incorrect; mass is not squared in Newton's second law.

question: As of March 2020, which of the following solar power plants is the biggest plant in the world, with total installed capacity of 2,245 MW?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhadla solar park.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of March 2020, the Bhadla Solar Park, located in Bhadla village, Jodhpur district, Rajasthan, was the world's largest solar power plant, with a total installed capacity of about 2,245 MW. (भड़ला सौर पार्क — राजस्थान, विश्व का सबसे बड़ा सौर पार्क)

 

• It spans roughly 14,000 acres and benefits from the region's abundant sunshine, minimal cloud cover, and low humidity — ideal conditions for solar power generation.

 

• It was developed in phases by multiple agencies, including the Rajasthan Solar Park Development Company Limited (RSPDCL), NTPC, and the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Indian solar parks include the Pavagada Solar Park (Karnataka) and the Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park (Andhra Pradesh).

 

• India has set ambitious renewable energy targets, aiming for 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel-based capacity by 2030.

 

NOTE

 

• Kamuthi solar power project (Option 1): Located in Tamil Nadu; was once (2016) the world's largest single-location solar plant (~648 MW), much smaller than Bhadla.

 

• Sakri photovoltaic solar energy project (Option 2): Located in Maharashtra; a considerably smaller solar plant.

 

• Dhirubhai Ambani solar park (Option 3): Located in Pokhran, Rajasthan, developed by Reliance; smaller in capacity than Bhadla.

question: Select the olfactory indicator from among the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clove oil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Olfactory indicators are substances whose smell changes in acidic or basic medium, allowing detection of acid-base reactions through a change in odour rather than colour. (घ्राण सूचक — लौंग का तेल)

 

• Clove oil, vanilla essence, and onion are common examples of olfactory indicators — for instance, the characteristic smell of clove oil or vanilla is masked/altered when mixed with a base.

 

• This is distinct from acid-base (visual) indicators like litmus, phenolphthalein, or methyl orange, which show a colour change.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Natural visual indicators include turmeric (turns red/brown in base), red cabbage juice/china rose extract (colour change across pH range), and litmus (derived from lichens).

 

• A universal indicator is a mixture of several indicators used to estimate the approximate pH of a solution across the full pH range.

 

NOTE

 

• Petunia (Option 1): Its extract acts as a natural acid-base (visual/colour-change) indicator, not an olfactory one.

 

• Turmeric (Option 3): A natural visual indicator; its yellow colour turns red/brown in the presence of a base.

 

• Cabbage juice (Option 4): Red cabbage extract is a natural visual indicator that changes colour across the pH range.

question: Which of the following committees was associated with Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dutt Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, constituted in 1967 under the chairmanship of Subimal Dutt, is popularly known as the Dutt Committee. (औद्योगिक लाइसेंसिंग नीति जांच समिति — दत्त समिति)

 

• The committee examined the working of the industrial licensing system under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, and found that licensing had disproportionately favoured large business houses.

 

• Its report (submitted 1969) fed into the identification of MRTP (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices) companies and contributed to the enactment of the MRTP Act, 1969.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dutt Committee's findings highlighted that a small number of large business houses had cornered a disproportionate share of industrial licences issued since 1957.

 

• Its recommendations contributed to India shifting toward anti-monopoly regulation via the MRTP Act.

 

NOTE

 

• Gadgil Committee (Option 1): Associated with decentralised planning and the 'Gadgil formula' for allocating central plan assistance to states, not industrial licensing.

 

• Hazari Committee (Option 2): Also examined industrial licensing around the same period (headed by R.K. Hazari), but the formally-titled 'Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee' is the Dutt Committee.

 

• Sen Committee (Option 3): Not associated with the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classical languages of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magahi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the time of this examination (July 2024), India had officially recognised the following as Classical Languages: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Kannada and Telugu (2008), Malayalam (2013), and Odia (2014). (शास्त्रीय भाषाएं — तमिल, संस्कृत, कन्नड़, तेलुगु, मलयालम, ओड़िया)

 

• Magahi, a language spoken predominantly in the Magadh region of Bihar, was not included in this list at the time of the exam.

 

• Note: In October 2024 (after this exam), the Government of India granted classical language status to five more languages — Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali — but Magahi still did not receive this status.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A language is granted classical status based on criteria such as antiquity of its early texts (1,500-2,000+ years), a body of ancient literature, and an original literary tradition not borrowed from another speech community.

 

• The Ministry of Culture administers the process of conferring classical language status in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Malayalam (Option 2), Kannada (Option 3), Odiya (Option 4): All three were officially recognised as classical languages of India well before this exam (in 2013, 2008, and 2014 respectively).

question: Select the natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gir forest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, located in Gujarat, is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) in the world. (गिर वन — एशियाई शेर)

 

• The Asiatic Lion is listed as 'Endangered' on the IUCN Red List, and the Gir forest population is the last surviving wild population of this subspecies globally.

 

• As per the 2020 Lion Census, the Asiatic Lion population in and around Gir stood at 674 individuals, reflecting consistent growth from sustained conservation efforts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Project Lion was launched by the Government of India to strengthen conservation of the Asiatic Lion and its habitat.

 

• The Gir ecosystem — a mix of dry deciduous forest, thorny scrub, and savannah — spans the Junagadh, Gir Somnath, Amreli, and Bhavnagar districts of Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Sundarbans (Option 2): The world's largest mangrove forest (spanning India and Bangladesh) and the natural habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger, not the Asiatic Lion.

 

• Kanha National Park (Option 3): Located in Madhya Pradesh, known for tigers and as one inspiration for Rudyard Kipling's *The Jungle Book*.

 

• Saranda forest (Option 4): Located in Jharkhand, one of India's largest sal forests, known for iron-ore reserves and elephants, not lions.

question: At which place did Raja Ram Mohan Roy form a reform association called Brahmo Sabha in the year 1828?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in Calcutta (present-day Kolkata) in August 1828, which was later renamed the Brahmo Samaj. (ब्रह्म सभा — कलकत्ता, राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• The Brahmo Samaj was a monotheistic reform movement that rejected idol worship and sought to eliminate social evils such as sati, child marriage, and caste-based discrimination, promoting rational, Vedanta-based religious thought.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is widely regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' (also called the 'Maker of Modern India') for his pioneering role in social and religious reform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ram Mohan Roy's efforts contributed significantly to the abolition of Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, enacted under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

 

• After Ram Mohan Roy, Debendranath Tagore led the Brahmo Samaj and gave it a more organised institutional structure.

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay (Option 2), Pune (Option 3), Madras (Option 4): None of these cities was the founding location of the Brahmo Sabha; it was founded in Calcutta, then the capital of British India.
